title: DatasetReportRenderer reads `report.filter` as a lenient alias for `runtimeFilter` — a key the strict spec rejects with an explicit rename suggestion
body:
Found while implementing #5047. Filed unassigned; that card is docs-only and explicitly must not change `plugin-report` behaviour, so this was recorded rather than fixed.

Measured on `origin/main` at `958d757`.

## The read

`packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx:1246`:

```ts
const outerFilter = mergeFilters(
  (report.runtimeFilter ?? report.filter) as Record< string, unknown > | undefined,
  runtimeFilter,
);
```

and the same alias per joined block a few lines below:

```ts
const blockFilter = mergeFilters(outerFilter, (block.runtimeFilter ?? block.filter) as ...);
```

`filter` is declared on the renderer's local `DatasetReportLike` interface, so it type-checks locally.

## Why this is a contract inversion, not a convenience

`filter` is **not** an authorable key. `ReportSchema` (`@objectstack/spec` 17.0.0) is `z.core.$strict` and rejects it — and the spec goes out of its way to name the replacement:

```
unrecognized_keys: Unrecognized key(s) on this report: `filter`.
  Did you mean `filter` -> `runtimeFilter`?
```

So the producer side is unambiguous and even ships the migration hint. The consumer then quietly accepts the rejected spelling anyway. The result is the shape this repo keeps closing over elsewhere (#5116, #5120, #5067, #5068): metadata that **cannot** be authored through the validated path still renders when it arrives by some other route, so the strictness the spec promises is not the strictness the runtime enforces.

It matters most for AI-authored metadata: a generator that emits `filter` gets a working report from this renderer and a hard validation failure from anything that parses the document first. Which one an author meets is a function of which path the document travelled.

## Deciding it needs the migration story, not a guess

Two readings, and they differ in what happens to stored documents:

1. **Drop the alias** — declared equals enforced; any stored document still carrying `filter` loses its scope filter (it renders unfiltered, which for a filtered report is worse than an error).
2. **Keep it as an explicit, time-boxed read** with a console warning naming the rename, and remove it on a stated release.

Either way `DatasetReportLike.filter` should stop being an undocumented equal-status alias. Not decided here — it is the same enforce-or-retire question the ADR-0021 migration story owns.

## Recheck

```
grep -n "report.filter\|block.filter" packages/plugin-report/src/DatasetReportRenderer.tsx
```

Related: #5047 (the docs half — the migration table there routes authors to `runtimeFilter`), #5116 / #5120 / #5067 / #5068 (same lenient-alias family).
